diyarbakirwalls.name: Diyarbakır City Walls
diyarbakirwalls.slogan: Black basalt, 82 towers and a city still wrapped in stone.
diyarbakirwalls.line: The walls run about 5.8 km around old Diyarbakır, and UNESCO listed them with the Hevsel Gardens in 2015.

hasankeyfkale.name: Hasankeyf Castle
hasankeyfkale.slogan: A cliff citadel that watched the Tigris for centuries.
hasankeyfkale.line: The citadel sits about 100 metres above the Tigris, and the Ilısu reservoir covered the old town below it in 2020.

ulucami.name: Great Mosque of Diyarbakır
ulucami.slogan: Basalt arcades and a courtyard that echoes Damascus.
ulucami.line: An inscription dates the Seljuk mosque to 1091-92, and its layout follows the Great Mosque of Damascus.

surpgiragos.name: Surp Giragos Church
surpgiragos.slogan: A silenced bell tower that rings again over Sur.
surpgiragos.line: Said to be the largest Armenian church in the Middle East, it won a Europa Nostra award in 2015 after restoration.

malabadi.name: Malabadi Bridge
malabadi.slogan: One stone arch, 38 metres wide, and rooms in its shoulders.
malabadi.line: Built around 1147-1154, its single span is 38.6 m, and small rooms in the spandrels sheltered travellers.
